$comment: Canonical matn identities for the hadith narrations the Golden Set accepts. A group names one narration (`same-report`) or one ruling, instruction, or stated merit given by different narrations (`same-ruling`); its members are the corpus rows that carry it through another chain or another report. Both relations gate citation validity: a cited narration that states the same ruling is a valid citation, and the map, not a single address, is the gate's unit of identity. A label resolves to its transitive component — every group the map ties to it through a shared label — so the required label's component, not one group, is what citation validity accepts. Every group states its `rationale`, because the two claims are not interchangeable and a reader must be able to tell whether a group says "another chain of this report" or "another report of this ruling". A label outside every group is its own identity, so it can never match another. A label may be claimed once per relation (a canonical may anchor both kinds of group); two groups of one relation may not share a label. Owner-signed gate data: adding a group or a member changes what citation validity accepts, and a wrong member of any group in a component widens the gate, so any member edit in a component changes what the gate accepts.

groups.rationale: One report — the Prophet's wudu, shown and described — narrated through different chains; wording differs, the operative content does not.
One instruction — eat with the right hand — narrated through different chains; the members state one operative rule.
One report — cleanliness is half of faith — narrated through different chains; the matn is one statement.

One report — the Prophet combining Maghrib and Isha while travelling — narrated from Anas through different chains (Yahya ibn Abi Kathir ← Hafsh ibn Ubaydillah ← Anas). 1110 is the follow-up chain Bukhari names in 1108's own matn ("وتابعه علي بن المبارك وحرب عن يحيى عن حفص عن أنس"), so the two are chains of one report. The Ibn Umar rows are different reports and sit in the same-ruling group.

Bukhari 1108 (Anas, through Yahya ← Hafsh) and these rows state the same ruling — combining prayers while travelling — under different chains and wording: Nasai 598 and Muslim 1621 are the Malik ← Nafi' ← Ibn Umar report, Bukhari 1109 and Muslim 1624 the Zuhri ← Salim ← Ibn Umar report, and Ibn Majah 1070 the Mu'adh ibn Jabal report of combining all four prayers at Tabuk. None of them is a chain of the Anas report; the same-report group beside this one carries the Anas chains, and a citation of either kind satisfies the ruling this question asks for.

One report from Abu Hurayra — a man asked who is most entitled to his good companionship, and the Prophet answered "your mother" three times, then "then your father" — narrated through the same lower chain ('Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa' ← Abu Zur'a ← Abu Hurayra) from different top links: Muslim 6500 through Jarir, 6501 through Ibn Fudayl, 6502 and Ibn Majah 2706 through Sharik and Ibn Shubruma, 6503 through Ibn Shubruma, and Ibn Majah 3658 through Sufyan. Wording varies: 6501 adds "then your nearest, nearest", Ibn Majah 3658 states the mother twice and closes with the nearest, and 6502/6503 carry the matn only by reference to Jarir's report. They are chains of one report, not different reports; the different reports of the same ruling sit in the group beside this one.

Bukhari 5971 (Abu Hurayra) and these narrations state the same ruling — the mother is owed precedence three times, then the father — under different reports: Abu Dawud 5139 and Tirmidhi 1897 are Bahz ibn Hakim ← his father ← his grandfather, answering "whom shall I honour?", and Ibn Majah 3661 is Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib ("Allah enjoins you to your mothers three times, then to your fathers, then to the nearest of kin"). Different companions and wording, each adding the nearest of kin after the father; none is a chain of the Abu Hurayra report. Ibn Majah 3657 states the same instruction but every grader grades it Daif, and Abu Dawud 5140 lists mother, father, sister and brother in one breath and is Daif by both graders, so neither is a member.

One report from Ibn Abbas — the Prophet sent Mu'adh to Yemen, and Allah obligated a sadaqah from wealth, taken from the rich and returned to the poor — narrated through the same lower chain (Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Sayfi ← Abu Ma'bad ← Ibn Abbas) from different top links: every member reaches Yahya through Zakariyya ibn Ishaq except Muslim 123, which reaches it through Isma'il ibn Umayyah. Wording varies ("sadaqah" and "zakat", "تُرَدُّ عَلَى" and "فَتُرَدُّ فِي"). Bukhari 1454 is Abu Bakr's zakat schedule — a different report and a different ruling — and is not a member.

One report from Abu Hurayra — whoever treads a path seeking knowledge, Allah eases for him a path to Paradise — narrated through the same lower chain (al-A'mash ← Abu Salih ← Abu Hurayra) from different top links: Abu Dawud 3643 through Zaidah, Ibn Majah 225 through Abu Mu'awiyah, Tirmidhi 2945 through Abu Usamah (2646's own link), and Muslim 6853 through Abu Mu'awiyah, whose Indonesian edition appends the Abu Usamah chain as well (the Arabic edition holds that chain as 6854). The matn varies in length — 2646 states the knowledge sentence alone, 225, 2945 and 6853 carry it inside the fuller report on relieving a believer's distress, and 3643 states it in the short form followed by the deeds clause ("whoever is slowed by his deeds, his lineage will not speed him up") — so the identity is the narration, not one wording. Different reports of the same ruling sit outside this group: Tirmidhi 2682 and Ibn Majah 223 are the Abu Darda report, and Ibn Majah 224 ("seeking knowledge is obligatory for every Muslim", from Anas) is a different narration that every grader grades dhaif.

One report — the Prophet took silk and gold, one in each hand, and said they are forbidden to the males of his ummah — narrated from Ali through parallel chains that share the lower links (Yazid ibn Abi Habib ← Abu Aflah al-Hamdani ← Ibn Zurair ← Ali), with wording variants and Ibn Majah 3595 adding "lawful to their females". It is not the Abu Musa report, which the same-ruling group carries.

One instruction — gold and silk are prohibited to the men of this ummah and permitted to its women — narrated from different companions through different chains: 5148/5265/1720 are the Abu Musa report and 3597 the 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr report. Ibn Majah 3590 is not a member: its matn reads «نَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ عَنْ لُبْسِ الْحَرِيرِ وَالذَّهَبِ وَقَالَ هُوَ لَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَلَنَا فِي الآخِرَةِ» — the prohibition, with "it is for them in this world and for us in the Hereafter" and no male/female clause — so it does not state the men/women ruling this group records. Nasai 5149 and 5160 are not members either: they state the exception ("إلا مقطعًا" — gold or silk in a cut piece is permitted), a different ruling.

One report from Ibn Umar — there is no envy except in two: a man given the Book who stands with it, and a man given wealth who gives it in charity — narrated through the same lower chain (al-Zuhri ← Salim ibn Abdullah ← Abdullah ibn Umar) from different top links: Bukhari 5025 through Shu'ayb, Bukhari 7529, Tirmidhi 1936 and Ibn Majah 4209 through Sufyan, Muslim 1894 through Ibn Uyaynah and Muslim 1895 through Yunus. Wording varies («الكتاب» / «القرآن», «قام به» / «يقوم به»); the operative content is one. The Abu Hurayra report (5026) is a different report of the same ruling, carried by the group beside this one.

One report from Uthman — the best of you is the one who learns the Quran and teaches it — narrated through the same lower chain (Alqamah ibn Marthad ← Sa'd ibn Ubaydah ← Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami ← Uthman) from different top links: Bukhari 5027 and Tirmidhi 2907 through Shu'bah, Bukhari 5028, Tirmidhi 2908 and Ibn Majah 212 through Sufyan (5028, 2908 and 212 omitting Sa'd), Abu Dawud 1452 through Shu'bah, and Ibn Majah 211 through Shu'bah and Sufyan. Wording varies («خيركم» / «أفضلكم»); the Ali report (Tirmidhi 2909) is a different report of the same ruling, carried by the group beside this one.

One report from Aisha — the one who recites the Quran proficiently is with the noble scribes, and the one who recites it with difficulty has two rewards — narrated through the same lower chain (Qatadah ← Zurarah ibn Awfa ← Sa'd ibn Hisham ← Aisha) from different top links: Bukhari 4937 through Shu'bah, Muslim 1862 through Abu Awanah, Abu Dawud 1454 through Hisham and Hammam, and Ibn Majah 3779 through Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah. Wording varies («مثل الذي يقرأ» / «الماهر بالقرآن»); the operative content is one.

One report from Abdullah ibn Amr — the companion of the Quran is told to recite and ascend, his rank at the last verse he recites — narrated through the same lower chain (Asim ibn Bahdalah ← Zirr ← Abdullah ibn Amr): Tirmidhi 2914 and Abu Dawud 1464 through Sufyan. The Abu Sa'id report (Ibn Majah 3780) states the same ruling through another companion and sits in the same-ruling group.

One ruling — reciting or learning the Quran carries merit, so a citation of another report that states it is a valid answer to this question — carried by different reports: Bukhari 5025 (Ibn Umar: the man given the Book who stands with it is one of the two envied); Bukhari 5027 (Uthman: the best of you learns the Quran and teaches it); Tirmidhi 2909 (Ali: the same ruling through another companion; retained although Tirmidhi's note calls its route weak, because the ruling is corroborated — its fold is sahih lighairihi — and its matn states the ruling); Tirmidhi 2910 (Ibn Mas'ud: a good deed for every letter recited); Bukhari 4937 (Aisha: the proficient reciter with the noble scribes, the struggling reciter two rewards); Muslim 1874 (Abu Umamah: recite, for the Quran intercedes for its companions); and Tirmidhi 2914 and Ibn Majah 3780 (Abdullah ibn Amr and Abu Sa'id: recite and ascend, rank at the last verse). None is a chain of the Abu Hurayra report (5026); the same-report groups beside this one carry the chains. A corroborated ruling may be carried by a weak route; grade alone excludes when the matn does not state the ruling. Ibn Majah 213 and Tirmidhi 2905 state a merit but both fold to dhaif (213's graders split, with the dhaif-wins fold governing, and 2905 is weak in every grader's reading), so neither is a member; Tirmidhi 2883, Bukhari 5015 and Bukhari 5020 state a specific surah's or a parable's merit rather than the reciter's, Bukhari 5023 and 5024 state what was permitted for the Prophet's recitation, and Bukhari 5031 and 5032 are instructions to preserve the Quran — none of those states this ruling, so none is a member.
